Below is a quick‑reference guide to all **federal Canadian public holidays** that create *long weekends* during 2023 – i.e., holidays that fall on a Friday, Saturday, Sunday, Monday, or Tuesday so that at least one extra day off falls between them and your regular work week.  
(If you’re looking only at “official” federal holidays, provincial/territorial variations will not affect the dates listed here.)

| Date | Day | Holiday | Long Weekend Pattern |
|------|-----|---------|-----------------------|
| Jan 1 | Sun | New Year’s Day | **Sun–Mon** (New Year's Eve & New Year's Day) |
| Apr 7 | Fri | Good Friday | **Fri–Sat** (Good Friday & Easter Saturday) |
| May 22 | Mon | Victoria Day | **Thu–Mon** (Victoria Day & preceding Thursday) |
| Jul 1 | Tue | Canada Day | **Tue–Wed** (Canada Day & following Wednesday) |
| Sep 4 | Thu | Labour Day | **Thu–Fri** (Labour Day & following Friday) |
| Oct 9 | Sat | Thanksgiving | **Fri–Sat** (Thanksgiving & preceding Friday) |
| Nov 20 | Fri | Remembrance Day | **Fri–Sat** (Remembrance Day & following Saturday) |

### How it works

| Holiday | Typical Long‑Weekend Scenario | Notes |
|--------|---------------------------------|-------|
| **New Year’s Day** | Falls on Sunday → You already have a full weekend plus New Year’s Day itself. | If you take Monday off, you’ll enjoy a four‑day break. |
| **Good Friday** | Always on Friday → Gives you a three‑day weekend if you don’t work Saturdays/Sundays. | Many employers give employees the next working day (Saturday) as a paid leave. |
| **Victoria Day** | Celebrated on the last Monday before May 25 → Creates a standard Monday‑off long weekend. | Some people also observe the preceding Thursday as a “pre‑holiday.” |
| **Canada Day** | July 1 fell on a Tuesday in 2023 → Employees who normally work Tuesdays often receive the following Wednesday off, giving a four‑day stretch. | In other years, Canada Day might land on a different weekday, altering the pattern. |
| **Labour Day** | First Monday in September → Classic Monday‑off long weekend. | A popular time for road trips across the country. |
| **Thanksgiving** | Second Monday in October → Another classic Monday‑off long weekend. | Often paired with a short trip to family or friends’ homes. |
| **Remembrance Day** | November 11 always observed on its calendar date regardless of weekday. In 2023 it was a Friday → Provides a nice early‑autumn break. | Observed nationwide, though many businesses close earlier than usual. |

---

#### Quick Tips for Your App Integration

1. **Calendar Sync:** Use the ISO‑8601 format (`YYYY-MM-DD`) for consistency—e.g., `2023-04-07` for Good Friday.
2. **Time Zone Awareness:** All dates above refer to the local time zone of the province where the holiday is celebrated federally. For apps spanning multiple regions, consider storing both UTC and local times.
3. **User Preferences:** Allow users to toggle whether they want to see *all* federal holidays or just those that generate extended breaks.
4. **Future Years:** Since most federal holidays shift annually (except fixed ones like New Year’s), keep a dynamic rule engine rather than hard‑coding future calendars.

Feel free to let me know if you'd like additional details—for example, provincial holidays that could extend certain long weekends—or help formatting this data programmatically!
